name: Soft Blue-Violet
lede: Soft Blue-Violet is a muted violet-blue built from modifier grammar, 'soft' plus Blue-Violet, and its hue already sat in Robert Ridgway's 1912 color atlas before anyone called it this name.

sections.title: An old swatch, a modifier name
sections.body:
Our graph names this color by modifier grammar, 'soft' added to the family word [[blue-violet]] [1]. Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature carried a close match on plate XXIII, hue 55′, and the ISCC-NBS system later classified that swatch in 1955 as block 206, a brilliant violet [2].

Our real nearest look-alikes are [[violet-blue|Violet blue]], clearly more vivid than this muted version, with [[middle-blue-purple]], almost the same hue, sitting a little further out still [3]. Two deeper modifier siblings sit further down the same family: [[deep-soft-blue-violet]] and [[deep-soft-bluish-violet]], both duller and darker than this version [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds only 3 paintings that match this violet-blue, as photographed, with the within-painting lens counting it in just 1 — rarer than 86 percent of the named colors we track [4]. Its one confirmed appearance is in Edvard Munch's 1901 work, where it plays an accent rather than a dominant field of color [4]. That single match is too thin a sample for any claim about century, country or painter beyond this one canvas [4].
